problems.title: Volume by circular slices
problems.question: The region under $y=(2x-1)^{50}$ between x=0 and x=1 rotates about the x-axis. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
steps: An antiderivative is (2x−1)¹⁰¹/202. Its values at 1 and 0 differ by 2/202.

problems.title: Distance from a cone centre to a generator
problems.question: A cone of base radius 2 has three pairwise perpendicular generators. Find the distance from its base centre to a generator.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
formulas: If θ is the generator angle to the base, $3\sin^2\theta=1$. The perpendicular distance is $r\sin\theta$.
steps: In the right axial half-triangle, this is the altitude from the right-angle vertex to the generator. Thus the distance is 2/√3.

problems.title: Two logarithmic limits
problems.question: Find (a) $\lim_{x\to\infty}\ln x/\sqrt[3]x$ and (b) $\lim_{x\to 1}(1-x+\ln x)/(1+\cos\pi x)$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
steps: For (a), 3x^(−1/3)→0. For (b), numerator =−u²/2+O(u³), denominator =1−cosπu=π²u²/2+O(u⁴). Divide and take the limit.

problems.title: One point meeting two plane conditions
problems.question: A=(1,1,0), B=(−1,2,8), C=(0,1,3). Find any point in plane ABC whose coordinates sum to 1.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
formulas: $AB\times AC=(3,-2,1)$, so the plane equation is $3x-2y+z=1$.
steps: Choose x=y=0. The plane then requires z=1, and the coordinate sum is also 1.

problems.title: An impossible single intersection
problems.question: The curves $x^2/a^2+y^2/10=1$ and $y^2=-12x$ supposedly have exactly one common point. Find the distance from the parabola focus to the ellipse directrix.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
formulas: Both equations are unchanged when y is replaced by −y. Any intersection with y≠0 therefore comes in a distinct pair.
steps: A sole intersection would have y=0. The parabola then gives x=0, but (0,0) is not on the ellipse. Thus no nondegenerate ellipse in the stated family can have exactly one common point with the parabola.
problems.answer: No such a exists; the requested distance is undefined.
problems.note: The single-intersection condition is inconsistent. Treating the two symmetric points as one would change the question.

problems.title: Cylinder chord distance
problems.question: Points A, B on the upper and lower base circles satisfy AB=$2\sqrt3$ and line AB makes 60° with the base. The cylinder volume is 42π. Find the axis distance of the vertical section through AB.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
steps: The projected segment is a chord of length ABcos60°=√3. Its half-length is √3/2. Thus d²=r²−(√3/2)²=53/4.

problems.title: The nearest graph point and its tangent
problems.question: B lies on $y=2\sqrt x$ and is closest to A=(5,0). Find the tangent at B.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
steps: The minimum occurs at x=3, so B=(3,2√3). The derivative is y′=1/√x, hence the tangent slope is 1/√3. Use point–slope for m and simplify.

problems.title: Integration by parts twice
problems.question: Find $\int x^2e^x\, dx$.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
steps: First choose u=x², dv=eˣdx: the result is x²eˣ−2∫xeˣdx. Apply integration by parts again to ∫xeˣdx=xeˣ−eˣ. Combine the terms.

problems.title: A logarithmic chord midpoint
problems.question: A, B lie on y=log₂x and have midpoint (6,2). Find the length of the projection of AB on the x-axis.
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
steps: The two x values are roots of t²−12t+16=0, namely 6±2√5. Their difference is the horizontal projection length.

problems.title: Does a maximum cylinder surface exist?
problems.question: A closed cylinder has volume 199 m³. What base radius gives the maximum possible total surface are a?
problems.idea: Translate the condition into an equation and check whether the requested object exists.
steps: As r→∞, the first term tends to infinity; as r→0⁺, the second does too. Thus surface are a is unbounded and has no maximum. Differentiation instead gives a minimum at 4πr−398/r²=0.
problems.note: If “minimum” was intended, the radius would be (199/(2π))^(1/3) metres, with h=2r. This is a different optimisation problem.
